name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.144.0 — The client player is a loop, not a form: a journey's state (unseen | walking | changes-requested | fixed | ok | waived) derives from the client's own requests in lib/mocks-walk.js, a new request on an OK'd journey takes the confirmation back into history, and the client accepts (Looks good) or reopens (Still not right, with their own words) an addressed request on the page. The index gains a "something missing?" composer and a request list; the CLIENT step prints whether the server is answering, each journey's state, and 📥 what the client left with the one command that answers each item — the session never starts, stops, or probes the client server outside that line, because it is the user's own long-lived process, kept running until approved. 7.143.0 — A repo's test count is now instrumented, not capped. `lib/scan-test-calls.js` is the one definition of a test case — a `test(`/`it(` call at line start across the host's test-classified files, blind to strings, comments and regex literals — and `count-tests.js` reports it (`tests: <count> cases`, `--json` → `{"count":N}`, never a non-zero exit for the count itself). The review's new `tests` leg records that count on every evidence manifest and is deliberately absent from every blocking set (`BLOCKING`, `REVIEW_BLOCKING`, `BLOCKING_LEGS`), so the number lands on each ledger row and can never redden a verdict. There is no limit, no ceiling file and no hook: `spec/test-ceiling.json` is deleted, and a count that could fail a build would make deleting tests the model's cheapest route to green. 7.142.0 — specs/20260910/05: exclusion rows are derived, never hand-typed — ledger derive turns discovery non-goals, no-answered invented rows, and not-needed note withdrawals into exclusion rows; the client confirms them one button each on a journey's last screen before --mark approved will run; --mark roadmap-written refuses any confirmed exclusion missing from the roadmap overview's Parking lot; and --mark approved writes design/mocks/exclusions.md, a dated file a statement of work can cite.
